clue.text: Drawers needed for board-games

definitions.meaning: people who draw technical plans or pictures
the pieces used in a board game played on a chequered board, called checkers in the US

explanation.definitionFit: Draftsmen make drawings, and in British usage the counters in the game of draughts carry the same name.

clue.text: An American lawman without charm maybe — and money

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American public prosecutor

indicators.note: maybe signals that the word charm is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A US law officer, lacking charm perhaps, is also short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; DA is the US District Attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece before the euro, so a form of cash.

clue.text: Little things to put in a piece of writing

indicators.note: the word to is placed inside the letters that follow, as the clue instructs

parts.note: MS is the standard abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: Advice to add small details to an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Particles of matter are the tiniest building blocks, hence tiny things.

clue.text: Sound visitor, so it's thought

indicators.note: the word as heard rather than as spelt, flagged by Sound at the front of the clue

parts.note: a visitor is a guest

explanation.surface: A trustworthy caller, or so people believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, describing the visitor, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reckoned something without being sure is to have supposed it.

clue.text: Willing to investigate at one point

parts.note: to investigate is to test
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Prepared to look into matters at some stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' reads as eager, but here it means making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies having made a will dies with a legal document disposing of property, a punning sense of the definition.

clue.text: Plans changes in most lowly form of life

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the word most
changes tells us the word Plans is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan undergoes alterations in a very humble organism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plans changes' reads as a sentence about plans being altered, but 'changes' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A moss is a simple, primitive plant, low on the evolutionary scale.

clue.text: Appearing in a tattered singlet is ingenuous in the extreme

indicators.note: tattered suggests the two short words are torn and reassembled

parts.note: a singlet is a vest, a sleeveless undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone shows up in a ragged undershirt and is utterly unworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearing' only links; a singlet is what British speakers call a vest, the sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most innocent and unsophisticated is the superlative of artless.

clue.text: Sailor taking drink around on "the sea-ear"

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: the drink wraps round the word on

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A seaman with a drink in hand stands by the ocean shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-ear is an old name for this shellfish, after its ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: A knockout in the theatre!

parts.note: a knockout sounds like a hit show, but the theatre is the operating theatre and the knockout is what renders a patient unconscious

explanation.definitionFit: A drug that makes a patient unconscious for surgery literally knocks them out in the operating room.

clue.text: Old poetry among the crassest in all respects

indicators.note: the letters are found among the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some ancient verse ranks as the very worst in every way.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'craSSEST IN All'; 'respects' only completes the surface phrase 'in all respects'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is a medieval verse form of six six-line stanzas, devised by troubadours.

clue.text: Clearly stated to be jointed

definitions.meaning: having joints or connected sections, like a lorry

explanation.definitionFit: Words expressed distinctly are said this way, and a vehicle with a hinged trailer section is described the same way.

clue.text: As the result of a bill, the man's suffering

definitions.note: the noun suffering stands for plural pains here

parts.note: A/C is short for account, a bill
the man is HE, so the man's is HE'S

explanation.surface: A man is in pain because of an invoice he received.
explanation.walkthrough: A/C, account, is a bill; 'As the result of' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull continuous pains are forms of suffering.

clue.text: Making inept pass, gets most irascible

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of the two words are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A footballer who passes badly becomes very short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: The most snappish person is the quickest to bite back, superlatively irritable.

clue.text: Main plant source of alginates

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
a weed is an unwanted plant

explanation.surface: The chief plant from which alginates are obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective meaning chief, but it is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Alginates, used as thickeners, are extracted from brown kelp.

clue.text: A rhetorical device, to put it mildly

definitions.text: A rhetorical device, to put it mildly

parts.words: A rhetorical device, to put it mildly
parts.note: the clue names a figure of speech and then describes exactly what that figure does: says something harsh in gentler words

explanation.definitionFit: A softened term substituted for a blunt or offensive one is a figure of speech for speaking gently.

clue.text: Stretchy lace — it's woven in a new way

indicators.note: weaving threads again in a new pattern signals rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Fabric lace that stretches has been knitted using a novel method.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that returns to shape after pulling is springy and extensible.

clue.text: For the woman wanting secure locks

definitions.text: For the woman wanting secure locks

parts.words: For the woman wanting secure locks
parts.note: locks sounds like door security, but the locks are tresses and the item fastens them in place

explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped pin holds hair in place, keeping tresses fixed.

clue.text: Builders can idle in this country

indicators.note: builders construct something new, here out of the letters of can idle

explanation.surface: Construction workers are allowed to laze about in this nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Builders' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic is a country.

clue.text: Offering no horse over a certain figure

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
on can mean over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: A bookmaker declines bets on any horse beyond a particular price.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometrical shape.

clue.text: Hint returning before autumn would present unexpected difficulty

indicators.note: returning means the word for hint is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a hint
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Advice coming back before the season changes would cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden danger or trap is an unforeseen problem.

clue.text: Object: to make a tiresome person admit corruption

indicators.note: admit means let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person
rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: The aim is getting a nuisance to confess to bribery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb, to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise an objection.

clue.text: Join together to get about in a Mediterranean island

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the two pieces that follow

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island in the Mediterranean
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Meeting up to travel around a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by accumulation, things fusing into one mass.

clue.text: Work out route, then get to it

indicators.note: work out signals solving the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Plan the route, then head for the destination.
explanation.definitionFit: An old legal word meaning to that thing or place, an archaic adverb.

clue.text: Passage about a coin that's no longer legal tender

definitions.text: coin that's no longer legal tender

indicators.note: the passage goes round the letter a

parts.note: a duct is a passage or channel

explanation.surface: A corridor around an obsolete piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold piece formerly used across Europe, now out of circulation.

clue.text: Follow many a precept laid down

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Obey numerous instructions that have been handed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine laid down as unquestionably true is an authoritative principle.

clue.text: Being persuasive and firm, making cuts

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
axing means cutting jobs or budgets

explanation.surface: A company trying to win people over while slashing staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Gently urging someone with flattery is persuading them.

clue.text: The pundit's urge to be in front

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
to head is to be at the front

explanation.surface: An expert commentator wanting to be the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual or learned expert is a highbrow authority.

clue.text: Show bad spirit — complain about a good man

parts.note: a demon is an evil spirit
ST, saint, is a good man
to rate is an old word for scold or rail at

explanation.surface: Displaying an evil temper by grumbling about a decent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only links; ST, for saint, is the crossword's good man.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit or prove something is to make it evident.
